rationale: Objective peak_allocated_bytes on the current accepted version (stem micro-batch rows8 + stage-0 micro-batch rows8, both verified executing in this discovery: stem Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU/max_pool2d n=4, copy_ n=4, one 32x64x56x56 assembly; stage-0 slices/Sequential/Identity n=4, add_ n=8) measures exactly 177,409,024 B = live FP32 params 46,758,048 + GPU-resident input 19,267,584 + retained workspace 8,622,944 + 4 x 25,690,112, where 25,690,112 is one 32x64x56x56 FP32 unit (also exactly 8x64x112x112). The previous parameter search measured stage0_chunk_rows=8 and =16 at the identical 177,409,024, so the binding moment is independent of stage-0 chunk transients; the peak now sits in a phase that parameter cannot touch. Static liveness bounds leave the unchanged stage-1 phase at <= base + 1 unit + 3-4 x 12,845,056 and the chunked stage-0 phase at ~ base + 2 units + 6,422,528 transients, both below the measured 4 units; the stem phase is the only phase where 3 x 25,690,112 coexist in the observed aten sequence (full assembly empty+4x copy_, chunk conv_out 8x64x112x112, chunk bn_out 8x64x112x112), with the fourth unit unexplained by static shapes (per-operator allocation attribution is an explicit unknown; plausibly cudnn workspace for the 7x7 stride-2 conv, which also scales with chunk rows). Halving the stem chunk is the one lever that shrinks every term of that phase: rows=4 turns conv_out/bn_out (and any row-scaled workspace) into 12,845,056 each while the assembly stays 25,690,112. The earlier stem parameter search already executed rows=4 cleanly (objective identical to rows=8 at 203,099,136 while stage 0 was binding), so the lever is proven executable and quality-passing. Selection: region scope re-binding the ResNetEmbeddings boundary (call d16297b8a11b79a2657853d0) with the same proven pattern at half chunk size, running the unchanged Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU/max_pool parents through context.references on contiguous row chunks and assembling one [32,64,56,56] FP32 tensor consumed unchanged by the untouched stage-0 bundle and stages 1-3; no functional dispatch sites, so the legacy direct-callable backend applies. All 32 stem-subtree groups are selected; the 49 additional calls (stage-0 assembly empty/copy_/slice calls and 43 record_function_exit family calls) are included only because those group families share ownership across the region boundary, matching the accepted region-selection precedent.
hypothesis: Re-binding the stem region at chunk_rows=4 (parameter space may probe 2/4/8) lowers peak_allocated_bytes from 177,409,024 B to approximately 151,718,912 B (-25,690,112, -14.5%): with 4-row chunks the stem-phase coexistence becomes assembly 25,690,112 + conv_out 12,845,056 + bn_out 12,845,056 + one further <=25,690,112 term (the statically unexplained unit, likely conv workspace that itself shrinks with rows), i.e. base 74,648,576 + 2 x 25,690,112 + 2 x 12,845,056 at worst. Even if the unexplained unit is fixed-size, the arithmetic lands exactly on 151,718,912; the graceful floor is the unchanged stage-0 phase (~145.3 MB: stage input + assembled output + 6,422,528 transients) and stage-1 phase (~151.4 MB), so no gain below ~145 MB is claimed. Throughput: constraint is images_per_second >= 7,158.9 (0.95 x 7535.66); the accepted version measured 8,506-8,538 img/s (16-19% headroom), rows=4 only adds four extra small conv/bn/relu/pool launches versus the accepted rows=8 route, and stem chunking has previously measured throughput-neutral, so the constraint is expected to hold. Numerics: identical per-sample FP32 kernels (eval batch_norm, out-of-place relu, max_pool2d, conv2d) on contiguous batch slices, the pattern already accepted twice with max_abs_error 7.6e-06 within atol=rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1; full 1000-class logits and predicted classes are unchanged. These benefit, throughput and numerics expectations are hypotheses to be tested by the evaluator's clean paired measurement.
